title: The Bronze Age Collapse of 1177 BCE

cards.h: In a few decades, half the civilised world went dark
cards.b:
Around 1200 BCE, the Mediterranean world was a rich, connected network of kingdoms: Egypt, the Hittites, Mycenaean Greece, Ugarit, Babylon. Within about 50 years, most of them were ruined.

The archaeologist Eric Cline called it the year civilisation collapsed in his 2014 book, 1177 B.C.

cards.h: The golden age before the crash
cards.b:
The Late Bronze Age was globalised. Copper came from Cyprus. Tin came from far away, perhaps from today's Afghanistan or Central Asia. Kings wrote to each other as 'brother'.

A shipwreck found off Uluburun (Turkey), about 1320 BCE, carried tonnes of copper and tin, ivory, glass and goods from many lands.
At Ugarit, clay tablets baked by the fire that destroyed the city preserve a letter. The king said enemy ships had come, his army and fleet were elsewhere, and the land was left helpless.

Egyptian carvings of Ramesses III (about 1177 BCE) show battles in the Nile Delta with foreign warriors in strange horned helmets and feather headdresses. Egypt called them 'Sea Peoples'.

Nobody knows exactly who they were. Names like Peleset (maybe the Philistines) appear. Some may have been refugees, not just raiders.

Evidence suggests drought and famine, earthquakes, internal revolts, and the breakdown of trade. When tin stopped, bronze was hard to make. A chain reaction followed, as the kingdoms depended on each other.

Egypt survived but was weakened. The Hittites vanished. Greece lost writing for centuries (the Linear B script disappeared).

From the ruins came new things: iron became common, the alphabet spread, and new small states appeared, such as Israel, Phoenician cities and Aramaean kingdoms.

Greece entered what is often called a Dark Age. But from it the city-states of classical Greece would later grow.

Older books blamed the Sea Peoples alone. Most historians now say it was a system collapse: many causes interacting. Some stress climate. Others stress politics. Some say 'collapse' is too strong, since many places continued.

The 'earthquake storm' idea, a run of earthquakes, is also disputed. No single explanation convinces everyone.

Five things to remember

  1. Late Bronze Age kingdoms were deeply linked.
  2. Around 1200-1150 BCE many collapsed.
  3. The Sea Peoples are named in Egyptian records but remain mysterious.
  4. Most historians blame several causes together.
  5. Iron, alphabets and new states followed.

Think about it

  • What does it say about us that connection makes us stronger and weaker?
  • Could a modern global crash happen the same way?
